newsitem.title: USA: US Texas/Okla, Kansas fed cattle sell $65, off $1.
newsitem.headline: US Texas/Okla, Kansas fed cattle sell $65, off $1.

text.p: U.S. feedlot cattle in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and in Kansas sold at $65.00 per cwt after midday Tuesday in light to moderate volume, down $1.00 from last week's top, feedlot sources said.
About 20,000 head sold in Kansas and about 10,000 in the Panhandle area, they said.
Several packers also reportedly dropped bids to $64.00-$64.50 from $65.00 once sales began, some sources said.
"Cattle started trading at $65 after the close and slowly picked up," a Panhandle source said, referring to sales after the close of Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures.

Fed cattle prices were pressured by a steep drop in boxed beef values at midday, which reinforced earlier perceptions that the cattle and beef markets appeared top heavy following last week's brisk sales at higher levels, the sources said.

Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.75 to $1.25 per cwt, with 165 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $107.66, down $1.25 from Monday, USDA statistics showed.
Weakness in fed cattle prices also was attributed to increased supplies of formulated and contract cattle that became available to packers after Friday, sources said.
